headline: Efficient CPU and distributed tools for single-cell and protein sequence analysis
label: Scalable Sequence Analysis Algorithms
summary: Datasets now reach 10M cells and billion protein sequences, making runtime, memory, and reproducibility central constraints for analysis tools.
synthesis: The shared thread is engineering throughput for sequence-scale data. brisc runs a multithreaded CPU single-cell RNA-seq workflow on 10M cells in 3 minutes and reports reproducible results across thread counts. The simpleaf extension quantifies probe-based multiplexed single-cell data at sub-gene resolution with lower runtime and memory than cyto and Cell Ranger. RabbitCD-HIT distributes greedy incremental clustering across billion-scale protein sequences, reporting a 2.1-6.6x speedup over CD-HIT. The new element is that these gains are reported alongside specific guarantees, namely thread-count reproducibility for brisc and high sensitivity for RabbitCD-HIT. The problems addressed differ across the three, and all three are currently preprints.
